category_title: Non-verbal students with moderate to severe cognitive impairments who respond to modified instrumentation and social reinforcement
minimal_context: Zack is sitting on the floor during a fourth-grade inclusive music class where the students are practicing recorder instruction and music reading tasks.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at the music notation and practice playing the notes on the recorder.

STUDENT: (Sits on the floor, lacking the fine motor coordination to cover the holes on the recorder or use his tongue to control articulation, and unable to decode the music notation.)

TUTOR: Try to cover the holes with your fingers and read the notes.

STUDENT: (Appears almost oblivious of what else is going on with the fourth graders, leaning back against a classmate's legs.)

TUTOR: Please focus on your instrument.

STUDENT: (Swipes the classmate's recorder cleaning stick and starts to play "keep away" with it.)

options.A: Provide melody bells placed on the floor that can be struck with the palm; use color-coded notation and paraprofessional assistance.
options.B: Provide positive reports home or positive feedback to the student's parents regarding his behavior and participation in music class.
options.C: Implement a Check-In, Check-Out (CICO) intervention where the student reports to the counselor, who serves as his mentor, each morning and afternoon.
options.D: Provide a clear beginning and end for each music reading task and recorder instruction activity during the class session.
